div.head: Rect 1.1
div.ab: [1.1] Eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne, swilce is deorhege to cyniges hame 7 scorp to friðscipe 7 sæweard 7 heafodweard 7 fyrdweard, ælmesfeoh 7 cyricsceat 7 mænige oðere mistlice ðingc.

Et de multis terris maius landirectum exurgit ad bannum regis, sicut est deorhege ad mansionem regiam et sceorpum in hostieum et custodiam maris et capitis et pacis et elmesfeoh (id est pecunia elemosine) et ciricsceatum et alie res multimode.

eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne swilce is. deorhege to cyniges hame 7 scorp to friðscipe . 7 sæweard 7 heafodweard 7 fyrdweard . æl|mesfeoh 7 cyricsceat 7 mænige oðere mistlice ðinge.

Eac of manegum landum mare landriht arist to cyniges gebanne, swilce is deorhege to cyniges hame and scorp to friðscipe and sæweard and heafodweard and fyrdweard, ælmesfeoh and cyricsceat and mænige oðere mistlice ðingc.

Auch erwächst von vielen Landgütern weitere Grundlast auf königlichen Befehl, wie [z. B.] ist Wildgehege für königliche Domäne und Ausrüstung zum Wehrschiff (Inlandflotte B) und See[küsten]wacht und [königliche] Leibwache und Landwehrwache, Almosengeld und Kirchensteuer und viele andere verschiedene Dinge.

Also from many estates further land-dues arise by the king's command, such as [e.g.] a deer-fence for the king's residence, and equipment for a warship (the home fleet, B), and coast-guard and [royal] bodyguard and army-guard, alms-money and church-scot, and many other various things.

Also, on many estates more land-right is originated at the king’s command such as, [to maintain] the animal-hedge for the king’s estate, and [to supply] equipment for a defence ship, and to guard the coast, and [to be a] head-guard and [to perform] military watch, [to give] alms money and church tribute and many other diverse things.

Furthermore, on many estates additional property obligations arise out of the king’s command, such as maintaining the animal hedge for the royal estate, provisioning a ship for defense, service in the coastguard, the royal guard, and the military watch, and the rendering of alms, Church dues, and many other various things.
div.note: The Quadripartitus read ‘landgerihte’. Leo corrected ‘friðscipe’ to ‘fyrdscipe’ after the Quadripartitus, which reads ‘frið’ for ‘fyrd’ five words later.
